findings.text: Ask 5 is not fully met: `Servex/agents/doc/own-page.md:14` still says both doors print "Your own page is /framework/ai/sessions/<id>/", and its rule section still calls that url the session's folder. That is the exact wording this task retired, in the doc `Servex/agents/readme.md:136` links as "how it learns its own page". Rewrite it to the dated-folder line (`Agents.folder_line`) and link `ai/sessions/doc/one-folder.md`.
Ask 5: `public/framework/ai/doc/agent-context.md:26` still says whoami gives "its page `/framework/ai/sessions/<id>/`". Change it to the dated folder.

A fresh agent can't pick this up from the task folder alone. `one-folder/task.jsonl` holds one line (the shots), with no open, log or landing. The "Next: fold the 1,410 old twins on the main tree" step exists only as a sentence in `requirements.md`. It is not filed as a task on the session record, so nothing will pick it up (CLAUDE.md law 10, "file each ask").

The comments in `.claude/hooks/prompt-relay.mjs:21` and `:239` still say the prompt goes to `sessions/<session_id>/page.jsonl`. The code at `:117` already uses the dated folder, so only the comment is stale. `Server/session-summary.mjs:14` has the same stale comment (`sessions/<id>/cache.jsonl`).

The `page_tools.js` PAGE_PATH description still ends "Omit it to mean YOUR OWN page, /framework/ai/sessions/<your agent id>/". As a route that is harmless, but it is the same flat-looking form the new rule warns against. The tool schema in this reviewer's own prompt shows it verbatim.

`agents.md` says to find the folder with `SessionFolders.at(store).of(id)`, while the hook and `Agents.folder_line` call `record_of(id)`. Both exist (`SessionFolders.mjs:115`, `:162`). The doc should say which one a writer uses and why.

The moved `239b0bd4` page shows "No tasks recorded under this folder" (shots/…/1920.png, band 3). The two moved `page.jsonl` lines (a log and a finish outcome) are kept on disk but drawn nowhere on the page, so the data survived the move but can't be seen. Not checked: whether "This session's page →" (the uuid url) redirects back to this same folder in a loop.
